headline: Transcriptomic risk models tie tumor immune states to prognosis and therapy response
label: Machine Learning Cancer Omics
summary: Public bulk and single-cell transcriptomes now yield prognostic gene signatures, often checked against immunotherapy response predictors.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning or multi-cohort inference from public bulk and single-cell transcriptomes to derive prognostic gene signatures and relate them to immune microenvironment composition and treatment response. Examples span a five-gene stromal-EMT signature in bladder cancer framed against checkpoint blockade and antibody-drug conjugate combinations, a four-gene READ-derived recurrence score in colorectal cancer, a 25-gene TCGA-LUSC model paired with TIDE, and THY1 linked to cancer-associated fibroblast infiltration. Wet-lab checks appear for selected candidates, such as CCT6B in hepatocellular carcinoma and RNPEPL1 in lung adenocarcinoma. What is new is the attempt to tie individual hub genes to specific cellular niches and therapeutic axes, for example MBNL2 with CAF crosstalk and poor response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, rather than reporting prognostic discrimination alone.
